svg.text: one row of A = 4 threads × float4
Each thread loads 4 floats (16 B) with
After one pass the block has loaded rows
and repeats: 4 passes cover all 128 rows.
Warp 0 always gets rows 0–7 of each pass,
so its data lands in As columns 0–7, 32–39,
As in SMEM, stored TRANSPOSED (16 × 128): A[r][c] → As[c][r]
128 (row r of A becomes column r of As)
Transposing means a thread's 4 consecutive floats go DOWN a column of As, so the
store can't be vectorized: 4 separate scalar stores (STS.32), with bank conflicts.
Worth it: the compute loop later reads ROWS of As with fast LDS.128 loads, many times.
